content_voiceover: This slide covers second line and beyond therapy for CLL and SLL. For second line or subsequent therapy, preferred options include BCL2 inhibitor regimens like venetoclax plus obinutuzumab, covalent BTK inhibitors such as continuous acalabrutinib or zanubrutinib, or the noncovalent BTK inhibitor pirtobrutinib for patients with resistance or intolerance to prior covalent BTK inhibitors. A footnote reminds us that venetoclax based regimens, with or without anti-CD20 antibody, or combined with a BTK inhibitor, are reasonable options for relapse after a period of remission. For patients who have already progressed through both a covalent BTK inhibitor and a BCL2 inhibitor, the preferred options shift to CAR T-cell therapy, specifically lisocabtagene maraleucel, a CD19 directed product, with or without ibrutinib, or pirtobrutinib if not previously given. Other recommended options at this heavily pretreated stage include PI3K inhibitors like duvelisib or idelalisib plus rituximab, lenalidomide, obinutuzumab, or alemtuzumab for deletion seventeen p or TP53 mutated disease. Chemoimmunotherapy combinations like FC plus rituximab or bendamustine plus rituximab are explicitly not recommended once a patient has deletion seventeen p or TP53 mutation.
keypoints: Pirtobrutinib, a noncovalent BTKi, is key after cBTKi resistance
CAR T-cell therapy with liso-cel is preferred after cBTKi and BCL2i both fail
PI3K inhibitors and alemtuzumab are later line options
Chemoimmunotherapy is avoided in TP53 mutated or del17p relapsed disease
keypoint_voiceover: After progression on a covalent BTK inhibitor, pirtobrutinib, a noncovalent BTK inhibitor, is a key next option. Once patients have failed both a covalent BTK inhibitor and a BCL2 inhibitor, CD19 directed CAR T-cell therapy with lisocabtagene maraleucel becomes preferred. Chemoimmunotherapy should be avoided throughout if deletion seventeen p or TP53 mutation is present.
